@tanstack/query/no-void-query-fn.reason: It needs type information, which oxlint JS plugins do not get, so it cannot run under oxlint.
@tanstack/query/no-void-query-fn.replacement: none (TanStack Query v5 rejects undefined query data at runtime, so tests catch it)

@typescript-eslint/explicit-module-bound.reason: TypeScript infers the types at module boundaries, and required annotations add churn without catching bugs.

@typescript-eslint/init-declarations.reason: Style only. tsc in strict mode reports use before assignment, and the rule forces placeholder values in patterns such as beforeAll setup and Promise executors.

@typescript-eslint/naming-convention.reason: Not in oxlint. Its boolean-prefix check needs type information, which oxlint JS plugins do not get, and many names it flags are fixed by external APIs or specs.

@typescript-eslint/no-invalid-this.reason: strict enables noImplicitThis, and uba/no-class keeps `this` rare.

@typescript-eslint/no-redeclare.reason: tsc already reports redeclarations, and the rule flags valid declaration merging, such as an interface and a const with the same name.

@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires.reason: Deprecated in typescript-eslint v8; no-require-imports covers the same cases.

@typescript-eslint/require-await.reason: It conflicts with promise-function-async on async stubs that must return a promise; no-floating-promises and await-thenable catch the real bugs.

@typescript-eslint/typedef.reason: Deprecated, and with no options every check defaults off, so it does nothing.

block-scoped-var.reason: Only matters for var; no-var is on and let/const are block-scoped, so it can never fire.

canonical/prefer-import-alias.reason: It matches paths against the folder the linter runs in (process.cwd()), so at a monorepo root a pattern such as ^src/ never matches without an override per package, and it skips export … from. A native no-restricted-imports pattern such as ^(\.\./){2,} does the check instead, without an autofix (see the README, Import alias).
canonical/prefer-import-alias.replacement: native no-restricted-imports pattern in the project's config

chai-friendly/no-unused-expressions.reason: Only needed for chai-style assertions such as expect(x).to.be.true. Its allow list can also hide an assertion with no matcher, which the native no-unused-expressions catches.

cypress/assertion-before-screenshot.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override.

cypress/no-assigning-return-values.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override.

cypress/no-async-tests.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override.

cypress/no-force.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override.

cypress/no-pause.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override. For Playwright, page.pause() is the equivalent.
cypress/no-pause.replacement: for Playwright: no-restricted-properties on page.pause in e2e files

cypress/no-unnecessary-waiting.reason: Not on: the Cypress option only loads the plugin, env and globals. A project that runs Cypress can turn the rule on in an override. For Playwright, page.waitForTimeout() is the same source of flaky tests.
cypress/no-unnecessary-waiting.replacement: for Playwright: no-restricted-properties on page.waitForTimeout in e2e files

default-case.reason: Forced defaults over TS unions become catch-alls that silently absorb new members; exhaustiveness checking is the typed replacement.

func-name-matching.reason: func-style declaration plus object-shorthand leave almost no named function expressions to check.

func-names.reason: func-style and prefer-arrow-callback already remove anonymous function expressions; nothing is left to name.

function-name/starts-with-verb.reason: Its fixed verb list misses common verbs such as mock and upsert, so it flags names that are clear. The convention is now a line in the AGENTS.md this package ships.

import/default.reason: In TypeScript files, tsc reports a default import of a module without a default export (TS1192).

import/export.reason: tsc already reports duplicate and conflicting re-exports (TS2300/TS2308); oxlint's version is nursery.

import/exports-last.reason: Layout preference with no autofix and no bug value; it only triggers lint-fix loops when agents export inline.

import/extensions.reason: tsc already checks TypeScript specifiers and .js specifiers are ignored; what is left are CSS and asset imports, which must keep their extension.

import/named.reason: tsc reports missing named exports (TS2305/TS2614); oxlint's version is nursery.

import/namespace.reason: tsc reports a missing member on a namespace import (TS2339/TS2694).

import/no-dynamic-require.reason: Only applies to require(); in TypeScript files typescript/no-require-imports already bans require() calls.

import/no-unresolved.reason: Typecheck already fails on unresolvable modules; oxlint deliberately does not implement it because of false positives.

import/no-unused-modules.reason: Without unusedExports or missingExports it checks nothing; if dead exports matter, knip checks them across the project.

import/no-useless-path-segments.reason: Cosmetic path cleanup with no bug value; nothing in oxlint or oxfmt replaces it, and nothing is lost.

import/prefer-default-export.reason: It conflicts with named exports, the common pattern in TypeScript code, so it mostly produces disable comments.

init-declarations.reason: TS strict definite-assignment checks (TS2454) catch use before assignment; the rule only forces needless initialisers.

max-nested-callbacks.reason: The default limit of 10 nested callbacks is almost never reached; complexity and max-depth cover the real nesting risk.

no-await-in-loop.reason: Sequential awaits in a loop are often deliberate: steps that must run in order, retries and backpressure. The rule cannot tell them from accidental serial work, so it mostly produces disable comments.

no-bitwise.reason: TS2447 already rejects | and & on booleans; the remaining uses, such as hashes and bit masks, are deliberate.

no-caller.reason: arguments.callee is a legacy pattern that throws in strict ES modules; agents do not write it.

no-const-assign.reason: tsc reports TS2588 on const reassignment; the lint copy only adds untyped JS files.

no-continue.reason: continue is often the clearest loop guard, and the rule catches no bugs.

no-delete-var.reason: delete on an identifier is a strict-mode SyntaxError and tsc TS1102; ES modules make the rule unreachable.

no-div-regex.reason: Purely cosmetic /=.../ ambiguity check; it guards no behaviour.

no-dupe-args.reason: Not in oxlint; duplicate parameters are a strict-mode SyntaxError and tsc reports TS2300.
no-dupe-args.replacement: tsc strict (TS2300 duplicate identifier; strict-mode SyntaxError)

no-dupe-keys.reason: tsc reports TS1117 for duplicate object-literal keys; the lint copy only adds untyped JS files.

no-eq-null.reason: eqeqeq 'always' already flags == null, so this rule duplicates it.

no-extra-bind.reason: Only flags .bind() on function literals that ignore this; with func-style declarations and arrow callbacks such code is rare.

no-extra-label.reason: no-labels already bans every label, so a redundant label cannot exist.

no-extra-semi.reason: Deprecated stylistic rule; oxfmt removes stray semicolons, and oxlint does not implement it.

no-func-assign.reason: tsc reports TS2630 when a function declaration is reassigned.

no-implicit-globals.reason: It only applies to script code; ES modules and CommonJS modules have their own scope, so it never fires there.

no-implied-eval.reason: For TypeScript files the type-aware typescript/no-implied-eval runs instead; the core rule would only add JS files.

no-import-assign.reason: tsc reports TS2632/TS2540 on assigning to imports.

no-inline-comments.reason: Trailing comments carry no bug risk; agents write them naturally, so the rule only adds rewrite loops.

no-inner-declarations.reason: Block-level functions are legal in strict ES modules and var is banned; oxlint's default also flags valid code that ESLint 9 allows.

no-invalid-this.reason: Not in oxlint; strict noImplicitThis reports untyped this (TS2683).

no-iterator.reason: __iterator__ is an obsolete SpiderMonkey property; TS rejects it as unknown on typed objects.

no-label-var.reason: no-labels bans all labels, so a label sharing a variable name cannot exist.

no-loop-func.reason: With let, const and no-var, a closure in a loop gets a fresh binding per iteration, so the bug it guards against cannot occur.

no-negated-condition.reason: Duplicate of unicorn/no-negated-condition, also on with the same check and autofix; running both doubles every report.

no-octal.reason: Legacy octal literals are already errors in strict-mode ES modules and tsc; oxlint deliberately does not implement it.

no-octal-escape.reason: Octal escape sequences are already errors in strict-mode modules and tsc; oxlint deliberately does not implement it.

no-plusplus.reason: Agents default to i++, so it forces manual rewrites to += 1 with no bug class once the formatter owns semicolons.

no-redeclare.reason: tsc reports redeclarations (TS2451/TS2300) and no-var is on; oxlint lacks ignoreDeclarationMerge and flags legitimate interface+const merging.

no-restricted-exports.reason: Without options it restricts nothing, and this package has no export to restrict; it is also nursery in oxlint. Turn it on with options in your config if you need it.

no-restricted-globals.reason: Without options it restricts nothing, and this package has no global to restrict. Turn it on with options in your config if you need it.

no-restricted-properties.reason: Without options it restricts nothing, and this package has no property to restrict. Turn it on with options in your config if you need it.

no-undef.reason: tsc reports undefined names (TS2304) in every TypeScript file; oxlint's version is nursery.

no-undef-init.reason: unicorn/no-useless-undefined, on in this config, flags let x = undefined; oxlint does not implement the core rule.

perfectionist/sort-array-includes.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-classes.reason: uba/no-class already keeps classes rare, and a sort order has no correctness value.

perfectionist/sort-decorators.reason: Decorator order can change behaviour, so an autofix that reorders decorators is risky.

perfectionist/sort-enums.reason: Sorting enum members has no correctness value, and member order matters for numeric enums.

perfectionist/sort-export-attributes.reason: Export attributes are rare and usually have one key, so there is nothing to sort.

perfectionist/sort-exports.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-heritage-clauses.reason: uba/no-class keeps classes rare, so implements lists with several interfaces are rare too.

perfectionist/sort-import-attributes.reason: Import attributes are rare and usually have one key, so there is nothing to sort.

perfectionist/sort-imports.reason: oxfmt sortImports, set up with perfectionist's default groups, orders import declarations on every format run.

perfectionist/sort-interfaces.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-intersection-types.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-jsx-props.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-maps.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-modules.reason: Alphabetical order fights top-down reading order, such as lifecycle order or a helper kept next to its caller.

perfectionist/sort-named-exports.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-object-types.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-objects.reason: Its autofix reorders literals where key order matters, such as objects whose key order is the output order, and TanStack Router route options, whose order @tanstack/router/create-route-property-order checks.
perfectionist/sort-objects.replacement: none (native sort-keys has the same hazard)

perfectionist/sort-sets.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-switch-case.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-union-types.reason: Dropped with the rest of perfectionist: a sort order has no correctness value, and every JS-plugin rule adds run time. oxfmt cannot do it (it sorts only imports, package.json and Tailwind classes).

perfectionist/sort-variable-declarations.reason: Statements with several declarators are rare in modern TypeScript, so there is nothing to sort.
perfectionist/sort-variable-declarations.replacement: none (native sort-vars exists if ever wanted)

promise/always-return.reason: In async/await code then callbacks are rare; demanding a return in each adds noise, and typescript/no-floating-promises catches floating chains.

promise/avoid-new.reason: new Promise is the right tool to wrap a callback API or build a deadline, so the rule mostly produces disable comments.

promise/catch-or-return.reason: typescript/no-floating-promises (type-aware, on in this config) catches unhandled promises more precisely, including async calls without .then.

promise/no-nesting.reason: Style rule about nested then chains; async/await code has no chains to nest.

promise/no-new-statics.reason: `new Promise.resolve()` is already a tsc error under strict (no construct signature), so the rule never fires.

promise/no-promise-in-callback.reason: Mixing styles is not itself a bug; the real hazard, an unhandled promise inside a callback, is caught by no-floating-promises/no-misused-promises.

promise/no-return-wrap.reason: Only checks Promise.resolve/reject wrapping inside then/catch callbacks, which async/await code rarely has.

promise/prefer-await-to-callbacks.reason: It fires on APIs that only offer callbacks, such as server.close() in node:http, stream events and zlib, where each report becomes a justified disable comment.

promise/prefer-await-to-then.reason: Without type information it cannot tell Promise.prototype.catch() from other .catch() methods, such as zod's schema.catch(); no-floating-promises covers correctness.

promise/valid-params.reason: tsc already rejects wrong argument counts to Promise.all/resolve/then (TS2554).

react/boolean-prop-naming.reason: UI libraries fix boolean prop names such as open and active, so it mostly produces disable comments; typescript/naming-convention is gone too.

react/destructuring-assignment.reason: Pure style; destructuring props in the signature is already the common pattern, and agents copy it.

react/function-component-definition.reason: func-style declaration with allowArrowFunctions: false already rejects named arrow components.

react/jsx-filename-extension.reason: tsc already rejects JSX in .ts files, and TypeScript projects rarely have JSX in .js files.

react/jsx-handler-names.reason: Default checkLocalVariables:false only inspects props.x/this.x handlers; components that destructure props are never checked.

react/jsx-no-duplicate-props.reason: tsc reports duplicate JSX attributes (TS17001) in every .tsx file; the lint rule only repeats it.

react/jsx-no-undef.reason: tsc reports undefined JSX identifiers (TS2304) under strict; the lint rule duplicates it.

react/jsx-pascal-case.reason: Components are PascalCase by convention, and tsc rejects a lowercase tag that is not an intrinsic element.

react/jsx-uses-react.reason: The new JSX transform needs no React import; the rule does nothing on React 19.

react/jsx-uses-vars.reason: oxlint no-unused-vars already counts JSX usage, so this ESLint marker rule is unnecessary.

react/no-adjacent-inline-elements.reason: Stylistic whitespace rule oxlint declines to port; it has no bug value.

react/no-deprecated.reason: React 19 types removed render/findDOMNode, so tsc fails them; typescript/no-deprecated covers the remaining @deprecated APIs.

react/no-did-mount-set-state.reason: Class-lifecycle rule; function components have no componentDidMount, and uba/no-class keeps classes rare.

react/no-did-update-set-state.reason: Class-lifecycle rule; function components have no componentDidUpdate, and uba/no-class keeps classes rare.

react/no-direct-mutation-state.reason: Class-only; Readonly<S> state already blocks field mutation in tsc.

react/no-find-dom-node.reason: React 19 removed findDOMNode and @types/react-dom 19 no longer declares it, so tsc fails any use.

react/no-invalid-html-attribute.reason: It only validates rel values, and oxlint has no port.

react/no-is-mounted.reason: isMounted exists only on the deprecated ClassicComponent type, so this.isMounted() in a Component subclass fails tsc.

react/no-namespace.reason: Namespaced tags like <svg:rect> are not supported by React and are rarely written.

react/no-redundant-should-component-upda.reason: PureComponent-only rule; function components have no shouldComponentUpdate.

react/no-render-return-value.reason: ReactDOM.render is gone from React 19 types, so tsc fails before any return value exists.

react/no-string-refs.reason: React 19 types define LegacyRef as Ref without strings, so string refs fail tsc.

react/no-this-in-sfc.reason: strict noImplicitThis makes `this` inside a function component a tsc error.

react/no-typos.reason: Checks PropTypes and class lifecycle spellings; TypeScript projects have no PropTypes, and the override keyword lets tsc check class method names.

react/no-unescaped-entities.reason: tsc already rejects > and } in JSX text; the remaining quote checks only force ' churn in copy.

react/no-unsafe.reason: Flags UNSAFE_ class lifecycles; function components have none, and uba/no-class keeps classes rare.

react/no-unused-class-component-methods.reason: Class-component rule that oxlint declines to port; uba/no-class keeps classes rare.

react/no-unused-prop-types.reason: oxlint does not implement it. no-unused-vars does not see members of a props type that are never destructured, so dead props can stay behind after a refactor.

react/no-unused-state.reason: Class-state rule that oxlint declines to port; function components keep state in hooks.

react/no-will-update-set-state.reason: Class-lifecycle rule; function components have no componentWillUpdate.

react/prop-types.reason: TypeScript props types replace PropTypes, which React 19 ignores entirely.

react/sort-prop-types.reason: PropTypes-only; TypeScript projects use typed props.

require-atomic-updates.reason: oxlint does not implement it, and it has known false positives on code that holds a lock, releases in finally, or runs in sequence.

storybook/await-interactions.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). Without them, the type-aware no-floating-promises still flags userEvent calls that are not awaited.

storybook/context-in-play-function.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). The rule only applies to play functions.

storybook/default-exports.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). Storybook's CSF indexer already rejects a story file without a default export.

storybook/hierarchy-separator.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). It guards against the old '|' title separator; current titles use '/'.

storybook/no-redundant-story-name.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). It is a cosmetic warning about a name Storybook would derive anyway.

storybook/no-renderer-packages.reason: Off even with shouldEnableStorybook so projects can choose their imports. Turn it on in an override to require imports from the framework package (for example @storybook/react-vite) instead of the renderer package.

storybook/no-uninstalled-addons.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). Storybook fails to start when an addon is missing.

storybook/prefer-pascal-case.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). Agents already name CSF story exports in PascalCase (Default) without being told.

storybook/story-exports.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). A story file with no stories fails Storybook indexing.

storybook/use-storybook-expect.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). The rule only applies inside play functions.

storybook/use-storybook-testing-library.reason: Storybook rules are opt-in (shouldEnableStorybook). The rule only applies to @testing-library imports in play functions.

unicorn/consistent-destructuring.reason: Not implemented in oxlint; pure style with known false positives, not worth a JS plugin.

unicorn/no-for-loop.reason: oxlint does not port it; typescript/prefer-for-of, on in this config, covers the same index loops.

unicorn/no-nested-ternary.reason: no-nested-ternary, also on in this config, forbids all nesting, so this looser unicorn copy adds nothing.

unicorn/number-literal-case.reason: It conflicts with the Prettier-compatible formatter on the case of hex digits.

unicorn/prefer-event-target.reason: Browser-portability rule; in Node code, a subclass of EventEmitter is correct, so the rule only produces disable comments there.

unicorn/prefer-json-parse-buffer.reason: Deprecated and unsupported in oxlint; TypeScript rejects JSON.parse(buffer) anyway.

unicorn/prefer-query-selector.reason: getElementById is safer for dynamic IDs; querySelector needs CSS.escape for them.

unicorn/prefer-reflect-apply.reason: eslint/prefer-spread already flags fn.apply(null, args) and points to the better spread fix.

unicorn/prefer-switch.reason: Not implemented in oxlint; if/else-to-switch is taste and not worth a JS plugin.

unicorn/prefer-ternary.reason: Lost its autofix in oxlint; forcing if/else into ternaries is taste with no bug value.

unicorn/prefer-top-level-await.reason: Without type information it reads other .catch() methods, such as zod's schema.catch(), as promise chains; no-floating-promises covers the real cases.

unicorn/prevent-abbreviations.reason: Not in oxlint, and not worth a JS plugin: it flags common names such as params and dir, and many come from library APIs.

vitest/no-conditional-expect.reason: It flags valid test code: TS narrowing such as `if (result.success)` after an asserted success, and branches in table-driven tests.

vitest/no-mocks-import.reason: It only checks imports from __mocks__ folders; tests that mock with vi.mock factories have none.
